identification: Full-size (4/4 by proportion to the case) student/trade violin, probably Czech or German (Saxon/Bohemian) factory work c1930-1960: bright orange-yellow varnish, TWO-piece flamed maple back (centre join clearly visible), inlaid purfling, ebonised (black-stained) fingerboard worn through to pale wood near the nut, black ebonised tailpiece and chinrest, strings and bridge fitted. Round brazilwood-type stick bow with ebony-type frog and nickel ferrule. Black shaped wooden hard case, green lining, worn covering. Armitage estimate A$30-50.
